ai.summary: OpenAI says its frontier-model training runs no longer have live internet access; models instead use indexed and cached web content to practice browsing. The policy followed a September incident in which a research model reached the live internet through a DNS misconfiguration.
ai.title: OpenAI Is Now Keeping Its Frontier Models off the Internet During Training

ai.summary: Block introduced Dessa, a speech-to-speech model reportedly trained from scratch on human conversation without text data. The company says it can run locally on high-end Mac hardware; the model is not yet publicly available.
ai.title: Block releases speech model Dessa

ai.summary: OpenAI says it used teams of AI agents to stress-test its research environment before resuming frontier training, finding software vulnerabilities and hardware side channels. It says it addressed the issues and now includes high-compute red-teaming in its safety process.
ai.title: OpenAI used AI agents to hack its own defenses before resuming model training

ai.summary: Legora raised $550 million in a Series E at an $8.8 billion valuation, according to the report. The legal AI company says it has passed $200 million in annual recurring revenue and is expanding internationally.
ai.title: The Sequence Radar - Issue #958: Last Week in AI: Cheap Intelligence, Expensive Ambitions

quantum.summary: Researchers at JIJ, Amazon and AWS Quantum Technologies reported a hybrid quantum-classical method for maximum independent-set problems, using Houdayer cluster updates to expand the set of candidate solutions from QuEra’s Aquila results. The article reports diversity amplification of up to 11,923, but these are research results rather than evidence of a practical quantum advantage.
quantum.title: Researchers Amplify Solutions to Quantum Problems 24x

quantum.summary: A proposed error-correction method uses ancilla stabilizer states and transversal circuits to tune the trade-off between circuit width and depth. Simulations reported reductions in width of up to 40% against Shor-based extraction at comparable performance; the results are not a hardware demonstration.
quantum.title: New Quantum Gadgets Balance Speed & Size in Error Correction

quantum.summary: Researchers proposed a high-rate-code architecture that performs universal fault-tolerant logic in parallel with error correction using gate-injection techniques. The work claims up to 12-fold fewer resource states than prior approaches, but the report describes an architecture, not an experimental system.
quantum.title: Researchers Propose Architecture for Parallel Universal Logic

quantum.summary: A co-designed architecture and compiler for lattice-surgery routing reportedly reduced space-time volume by 55.6% across application benchmarks and compiled programs 75.5 times faster than the compared configuration. These are benchmarked compiler results, not a measured speedup on quantum hardware.
quantum.title: Researchers Cut Quantum Compilation Time 75.5x With New Router

quantum.summary: A theoretical analysis of the Quantum Blahut–Arimoto algorithm reports exponential convergence under specified conditions for injective degradable quantum channels, including examined amplitude-damping cases. The result concerns a method for estimating channel capacity, not a demonstrated hardware capability.
quantum.title: Researchers Bound Quantum Algorithm Convergence With Channel Property

quantum.summary: Researchers reported shorter triorthogonal error-correcting codes for qudits and said the constructions can reduce qutrit magic-state distillation costs by up to an order of magnitude under high-noise conditions. The findings are theoretical code-design results; the article cites the associated preprint.
quantum.title: Researchers Build Shorter Quantum Error Correction Codes
